diezyxhao-baileys 1.3.3 — MALICIOUS

Sample: diezyxhao-baileys-1.3.3.tgz
SHA256: 1f17be251769f0d018e08adabe78f8181b12659ac74953a7eeeeb12c39eda698
This is a republished Baileys WhatsApp Web library, with interactive-message
builders, media processing, newsletter management, and a Telegram adapter.

Decisive behavior and version comparison
---------------------------------------
Fetched original npm releases 1.3.2, 1.3.1 and 1.1.23 with forager. Downloads
and .forage.json provenance are under scratch/version-drift/npm. The exact
predecessor described by the queue was not identified by version; the fetched
releases refute treating earlier releases as a trusted behavior baseline.

The two relevant modules in 1.3.2 and 1.3.3 are byte-identical:
  lib/Utils/channel-manager.js
    d5a9b1a5e17adf2c0ae790d8a91dbfe5ec491dfe1674dd2f36a5e315395403c1
  lib/Socket/newsletter.js
    16c911b56e9d45e6415661d3e1327e7959be8f3f540a4c25d144f582f5b562c4
1.3.1 has these same module hashes. Even 1.1.23 forces the same developer
channel in autoFollowAll; its constructor installs the open listener more
broadly. Current rules detect this earlier release too.

lib/index.js exports the ordinary makeWASocket factory. Its registration ->
business -> messages-recv -> messages-send layers reach makeNewsletterSocket.
That factory defaults customChannels to DEFAULT_UPDATE_CHANNEL and constructs
a ChannelManager using the active authenticated socket. It also schedules
tryFollow after 15 seconds and retries failures at increasing delays.
ChannelManager's constructor registers a connection.update listener for a
nonempty follow list. On open it calls autoFollowAll, which unconditionally
adds DEFAULT_CHANNEL to a copy of the caller's list. This occurs even when the
caller supplied entirely different targets. Removing or clearing the list
cannot exclude the hardcoded target from autoFollowAll. Setting
config.autoFollowChannels=false prevents automatic activation.

The effect reaches either newsletterFollow(targetJid) or a query stanza with
w:mex, query_id 7871414976211147 and newsletter_id: targetJid. Types/Newsletter.js
independently maps this numeric operation to FOLLOW. With the original inner
socket lacking newsletterFollow, the manager's fallback issues the same
protocol query. These are operations through the user's paired session, not
merely channel strings or declarations.

The 1.3.3 diff adds HTML-app and A2UI builders, associated message-edit and
business-stanza handling, exports and type declarations. Dependencies are
unchanged; an old next-swc native build artifact and license file disappear.
The forced-follow modules did not change. There is no evidence here that a
new maintainer-account compromise introduced this behavior in 1.3.3.

The README advertises auto-follow generally, and the socket logs an opt-out.
That does not authorize adding the publisher's channel to the consumer's
explicit custom list. This forced promotional effect tips the balance toward
MALICIOUS. Account-holder consent and actual deployment configuration are not
provided; runtime success against WhatsApp was not observed.

Other reviewed paths
--------------------
The source is readable JavaScript. Base64/hex/base32 helpers decode supplied
values and media; there is no recovered hidden script or downloaded executable
stage. Media shell execution invokes ffmpeg for video thumbnails. The Telegram
adapter uses a caller-supplied bot token and destination. The new HTML helper
inspects supplied markup, constructs sizing/scroll scripts and sends caller
content. The album helper's newsletter attribution uses caller options; its
large forwarding fields do not establish a separate hostile attribution graft
(their protobuf placement is also distinct from supported contextInfo fields).
These capabilities retain their accurate existing notable detections. No
supported additional credential-theft, C2, persistence or destructive action
was established. Parser flow limitations were supplemented by direct source
tracing and isolated execution of the relevant modules.

Correction
----------
Expanded the neutral whatsapp-newsletter-follow-query matcher from zero/one
qualifier before FOLLOW to zero through three. It now accepts the compiled
Types_1.QueryIds.FOLLOW spelling as well as QueryIds.FOLLOW and bare FOLLOW.
The comma and word boundary remain required. The matcher retains source-text
scope because runtime-patch consumers inspect code embedded in strings.
No rule was removed, weakened, relocated or demoted; no sample name or channel
identifier was added. Existing timer and supply-chain composites now activate.
The existing forced-default connection-open hostile trait remains intact.
Consumers were inspected in the social-manipulation and runtime-patch rules.
The new archive hostile composite's reported precision is 6.7.

Coverage and classifier comparison
----------------------------------
Counts below are unique trait IDs per archive/member, not sums of inherited
findings. H=hostile, S=suspicious.
  1.3.3 archive:             H 1 -> 2; S 0 -> 1; notable 307 -> 308
  Utils/channel-manager.js: H 1 -> 1; S 0 -> 0
  Socket/newsletter.js:      H 0 -> 0; S 0 -> 1
No findings were lost in any archive member. Newly present:
  micro-behaviors/communications/messaging/channel::whatsapp-newsletter-follow-query
  objectives/impact/ui/manipulation/social::timer-scheduled-default-channel-auto-follow
  objectives/supply-chain/trojanized/library/fork-branding::whatsapp-library-fork-timer-default-channel-follow
The timer path's missing detection is now covered; a third distinct hostile
behavior was not supported. Adding another copy of forced following solely to
meet the 3–5 goal would duplicate evidence rather than close a behavior gap.

Local atomscan ML probability: 0.9411947 -> 0.97969013; level stays -1.
An explicit terminal rescan reports all clean despite the hostile rule hits.
This is a remaining classifier miss, not grounds to erase accurate behavior
or inflate the score. The scanner reports model feature schema v18 vs v21;
this observation alone does not establish the cause of the classifier miss.
The 1.3.2 rescan also has H=2/S=1; 1.1.23 has H=1/S=0.

  following; complete JSON reports saved in scratch/version-drift.
- cleave facts for the archive and both relevant modules, including literal,
  text and flow views; no hidden executable layer was identified.
- check.py: nine selector/caller-config controls passed outside testdata.
- Existing baileys-hex-stage-review/check.py: 15 controls passed, including

- Isolated QuickJS execution: six socket traces across 1.3.2 and 1.3.3 passed
  (default, custom-list, disabled). Requires and every network operation were

- git diff --check passed. Final make validate is run after this record and
